engagement_background.objective: Generate meaningful procurement cost savings and enterprise value for APDerm by leveraging enterprise-wide purchasing power across fragmented, multi-site spend, thereby supporting Waud Capital’s value-creation plan during a period of inflation and supply-chain pressure.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Two-phase strategic sourcing program covering approximately $6.3 million in annual addressable spend across 10+ indirect spend categories (e.g., medical supplies, employee benefits, office supplies, small parcel, courier, IT hardware/software, telecom). Activities included competitive RFPs, incumbent negotiations, and use of Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) contracts; no clinical revenue-generating procedures were in scope.
constraints_challenges: Fragmented supply base and decentralized buying across numerous New England clinic locations acquired over time
Limited spend visibility and multiple uncoordinated supplier contracts, making baseline creation difficult
Inflationary market conditions and pandemic-related supply-chain disruptions driving rising input costs
Need to preserve service quality and minimize operational disruption, keeping most business with incumbent vendors
Requirement to obtain detailed usage data from suppliers where complete historical data was often unavailable or slow to retrieve

procurement_environment.data_availability: Accounts-payable spend data and some supplier contracts could be pulled from internal systems, but no centralized repository; detailed SKU/usage data had to be requested from high-spend suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Spend data lacked standard vendor naming; historical line-item data incomplete—engagement allowed for representative samples after six weeks of supplier outreach.
